title: ReZG: Retrieval-Augmented Zero-Shot Counter Narrative Generation for Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper evaluates Large Language Models on their ability to generate effective, relevant, non-toxic, and persuasive counter-narratives against hate speech directed at various marginalized groups, including religious groups such as Jews and Muslims. The evaluation measures metrics like Relevance (Rel.), Success Rate of Countering (SROC), toxicity, persuasiveness, and informativeness in a zero-shot setting.
findings: The paper found that the proposed Retrieval-Augmented Zero-shot Generation (ReZG) method successfully generated specific and effective counter-narratives against hate speech targeted at various groups, including Muslims and Jews. In out-of-domain tests, the method demonstrated strong generalization capabilities, significantly outperforming existing supervised and zero-shot baselines (like GPT2 and T0) in relevance and countering success rate (SROC) when defending these religious groups.
